identity.name: Sodium lactate
identity.chemical_class: Lactate salt (sodium salt of lactic acid)

function.mechanism: Acts as an organic-acid salt to help control pH and water activity; in formulated foods it can suppress growth/survival of target microbes depending on matrix and dose.
common_food_categories: other processed foods under GMP where moisture/pH control is needed

adi.basis: No finalized EFSA ADI found for E325 because EFSA re-evaluation question EFSA-Q-2011-00600 is still ongoing with no output posted.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA OpenEFSA record states E325 is already authorised in the EU and under delayed re-evaluation; phase is Ongoing Risk Assessment (updated 2026-01-19).

fda.notes: Permitted under current good manufacturing practice; regulation does not authorize use in infant foods and infant formulas.

adi.basis: ADI not limited (JECFA database and WHO Food Additives Series 5 context).

concerns.summary: Infant-specific concern is tied to historical D(-)/DL-lactic acid utilization limits; JECFA monograph cautions against D(-)/DL-lactic acid in infant foods, and US CFR separately excludes sodium lactate use in infant foods/formulas.

Recent food-microbiology work shows preservative-specific adaptation effects in Salmonella under subinhibitory exposure (including sodium lactate), but reported no antibiotic cross-resistance selection.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA lists ADI as not limited for sodium lactate solution.
EFSA re-evaluation record indicates additive remains authorised while reassessment is pending.
A 2024 preservative adaptation study did not find antibiotic cross-resistance selection after sodium-lactate-inclusive preservative exposure.

populations: infants (use-restricted population rather than ADI exceedance population)
adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric JECFA ADI cap (not limited). Current EFSA E325 reassessment is pending and does not yet provide a finalized updated exposure/ADI conclusion.

risk_assessment.rationale: Longstanding approvals (US GRAS and JECFA ADI not limited), endogenous lactate metabolism, and lack of strong modern human-harm signals support low concern under authorized uses. The tier is kept at limited (not risk_free) due unfinished EFSA re-evaluation and infant-related caution context.
key_factors: 21 CFR 184.1768 GRAS with GMP conditions and infant-use exclusion
JECFA ADI not limited (evaluation year listed as 1974)
EFSA E325 re-evaluation ongoing with no final output yet
Recent studies are mainly food-system microbiology, with no clear chronic human toxicity signal specific to dietary E325
